title: What are the degree measures of the four angles at X?
description: Four angles at the vertex X are measured with a protractor, always starting the count from zero on one arm. The angle BXC is also found by taking one reading away from another, and a direct measure checks it.
teaching_notes: One idea: the count starts from zero on the arm that lies on the zero line, and two readings from the same zero can be subtracted. Watch for students who read from the wrong arm.

source: Figure it Out (after Angle Bisector), Q6
video_script.why: The child measures angles at one vertex by the three checks of the solved example, and finds one angle by taking one reading away from another.
video_script.substitution: The angles BXE, CXE, AXB and BXC of the book's question.
video_script.anchor: the book's drawing of the arms XA, XB, XC and XE from the vertex X
video_script.payoff_line: Angle bee ex ee measures one hundred and fifteen degrees

final_answer.spoken: one hundred and fifteen, eighty five, sixty five and thirty degrees

maths_rules: angle BXC = angle BXE - angle CXE = 115 - 85 = 30 degrees
check: angle BXC + angle CXE = 30 + 85 = 115 = angle BXE
the count starts at 0 on the arm that lies on the zero line
video_script.design: The drawing stays on the board. The protractor is placed at X for each angle by the same steps, and one angle is found by subtraction; the readings are held back until the answer line.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the arms XA, XB, XC and XE drawn from the vertex X

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears, with the four arms drawn from X
marks.names: the four angles BXE, CXE, AXB and BXC are named one by one with small arcs
marks.ask: a question mark appears over the arms

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, with four angles at the vertex ex.
<bookmark mark='names'/>They are bee ex ee, see ex ee, eigh ex bee and bee ex see.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Before we measure, which of the four looks the widest?

beats.on_screen: the arms and angles stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a protractor with its centre point and zero line marked, next to the vertex X

marks.way: the protractor appears next to the vertex X
marks.zero: the zero line lights up and the scale that starts there is circled

beats.colours: centre in gold, zero line in green
narration: <bookmark mark='way'/>We measure the way the example in your book showed.
<bookmark mark='centre'/>The centre of the protractor goes on the vertex.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>One arm goes along the zero line, and we read the scale that starts at that zero.

beats.on_screen: Given: the angles BXE, CXE, AXB and BXC, all at the vertex X

marks.given: the four angle names are listed under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four angles at the vertex ex, with their arms drawn.

beats.on_screen: To find: the degree measures of ∠BXE, ∠CXE, ∠AXB and ∠BXC
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the degree measure of each of the four angles.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: put the centre of the protractor on the vertex X

marks.centre: the protractor slides until its centre point meets X
marks.why: a tick appears beside the centre point

beats.moves_through: the protractor slides onto the vertex
narration: <bookmark mark='centre'/>Step one, put the centre of the protractor exactly on the vertex ex.
<bookmark mark='why'/>All four angles have their vertex there, so the centre stays there.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: turn the protractor until the arm XA lies along the 0 line

marks.turn: the protractor turns until the arm XA meets the zero line
marks.scale: the scale that starts at that zero is circled

beats.moves_through: the protractor turns about the vertex
narration: <bookmark mark='turn'/>Step two, begin with angle eigh ex bee.
Turn the protractor until the arm ex eigh lies along the zero line.
<bookmark mark='scale'/>We read the scale that starts at that zero.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: read the number where the arm XB crosses the scale; measure ∠BXE and ∠CXE in the same way

marks.read: the arm XB is followed out to the scale and the mark it crosses lights up
marks.again: the protractor turns to the angles BXE and CXE, each time with its first arm on the zero line

beats.moves_through: the protractor turns for each angle
narration: <bookmark mark='read'/>Step three, follow the arm ex bee out to the scale and read the number.
<bookmark mark='again'/>Measure angle bee ex ee and angle see ex ee in the same way.
Each time, count from zero on the first arm.

marks.other: the angle BXC is lit up inside the angle BXE
marks.take: the angle CXE is cut away from the angle BXE and the part that is left is BXC

narration: <bookmark mark='other'/>Step four, find angle bee ex see another way.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Take angle see ex ee away from angle bee ex ee.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: measure ∠BXC directly; it must agree with ∠BXE − ∠CXE

marks.direct: the protractor is placed on the angle BXC
marks.match: a tick appears when the direct reading agrees with the subtraction

narration: <bookmark mark='direct'/>Step five, check by measuring angle bee ex see directly.
<bookmark mark='match'/>It must give the same number as the subtraction.

marks.ans: the reading of BXE is boxed
marks.second: the reading of CXE is boxed
marks.third: the reading of AXB is boxed
marks.fourth: the subtraction for BXC is written and its result is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Angle bee ex ee measures one hundred and fifteen degrees.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Angle see ex ee measures eighty five degrees.
<bookmark mark='third'/>Angle eigh ex bee measures sixty five degrees.
<bookmark mark='fourth'/>Angle bee ex see measures thirty degrees, which is one hundred and fifteen minus eighty five.
